transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martin (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Ava Patel (CTO, Zenith), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Jordan Kim (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary: quick intro, quickstart walkthru, hosted vs dedicated discussion, security questions, next steps + POC agreement

00:00 Sophie Martin: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm sophie from redwood, ae on the account, welcome.
00:05 Ava Patel: hi, thanks, we just got your invite. i am ava, cto, we'll probably be leaning on marco and jordan for the technical stuff.
00:10 Liam Chen: hi all, liam here, i'll run through the quickstart and some perf bits, and jump into dedicated/private stuff when needed.
00:22 Marco Ruiz: great, curious mostly about time-to-first-token, how fast can we go from signup to a working inference for our product?
00:30 Sophie Martin: totally. our PLG quickstart is designed for that — self-serve sign up, free credits, SDKs. typical time to first token for a standard text gen flow is under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart — create an API key, paste in a small prompt and you're streaming responses.
00:42 Marco Ruiz: okay, and does that include onboarding of models or do you host models?
00:48 Sophie Martin: we host a model catalog in the hosted API. you can use open models we've verified or bring your own via private deployment later. for quickstart you use the hosted models — lower friction.
00:58 Jordan Kim: what's the rate limits on the free credits? do we hit throttles quickly in early integration?
01:05 Liam Chen: free credits give you enough tokens to run a small bench. rate limits are standard sandbox levels but you can request higher limits — if you need load testing we can temporarily bump or put you on a dedicated pilot.
01:20 Ava Patel: can you explain the dedicated offering briefly? we're interested if our latency SLOs require it.
01:27 Liam Chen: dedicated is reserved GPU capacity — pools that you commit to, predictable throughput and lower noisy-neighbor variance. good for steady production throughput and strict latency SLAs. Hosted is multi-tenant, easy to start with, cost-effective; dedicated is when you need predictability.
01:45 Marco Ruiz: latency numbers — any sample for 8k context, 1k tokens?
01:50 Liam Chen: rough numbers off similar customers: hosted using an optimized 8k open model we see p50 token latency in the 40-80ms range depending on batch size and prefix caching; dedicated can be tuned lower with pinned GPUs and special kernel selection. i'll share the benchmark sheet after.
02:05 Ava Patel: okay that's helpful. data residency and compliance — we handle regulated data, need SOC2 and customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and VPC peering if possible.
02:16 Sophie Martin: yep, we have SOC2, we support KMS integrations and audit logs in Redwood Private or Dedicated with private control plane; Hosted can also integrate with KMS for encryption at rest and we have enterprise logs — that said for strict VPC-only flows our private/VPC deployment is the path.
02:31 Jordan Kim: is the private deployment on-prem only or VPC option for cloud?
02:35 Liam Chen: both — VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed networking, or an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. some customers start hosted, then move to dedicated or private for compliance.
02:47 Marco Ruiz: are there any common pitfalls when moving from quickstart to dedicated? like retraining prompts, config changes?
02:53 Sophie Martin: great question — the API surface is consistent, so prompt changes are minimal. main differences are model variants, quantization profiles, and batch tuning. we recommend a canary rollout and some evals to check regression.
03:10 Ava Patel: cost — what's the unit economics? if we use hosted for inference-heavy endpoints, cost could be high. do you provide cost tooling?
03:18 Sophie Martin: yes, Redwood Optimize gives suggestions (batching, caching, quantization) and the console shows per-token cost breakdown. for heavy workloads Dedicated with reserved capacity usually reduces per-token costs. we'll show a cost comparison for your expected qps.
03:30 Marco Ruiz: technical — do you support KV cache warmup and prefix caching? our use case has long-lived contexts and many repeated prefixes.
03:38 Liam Chen: yes, runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. you can configure caching policies, and there's automatic prefix caching for repeated contents which helps latency and cost.
03:48 Ava Patel: legal/procurement — contract length for dedicated, SLAs?
03:52 Sophie Martin: dedicated is typically monthly/annual reserved contracts with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. we'll route legal to our contracts team for terms.
04:02 Jordan Kim: regarding SSO, RBAC, and audit — is SAML supported?
04:07 Sophie Martin: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, full RBAC in the console, audit logs available for enterprise tiers.
04:14 Marco Ruiz: any experience with large context models and memory footprint? quantization options?
04:20 Liam Chen: we support quantization-friendly execution paths and recommend model variants per workload. for very large contexts we do kernel selection and memory management — we can advise on quantization (8-bit/4-bit) tradeoffs.
04:35 Ava Patel: who would be our point of contact for a pilot and bench runs?
04:38 Sophie Martin: i'll be AE, liam will run the bench and help with perf tuning. we'll give you free credits to run quickstart and then schedule a SE-led bench run to evaluate your actual prompts and latency.
04:50 Marco Ruiz: sounds good. i'd like to see a sample bench for our prompt distrib — and a cost estimate if we go hosted vs dedicated with 100 qps steady.
04:58 Liam Chen: noted, i'll prepare a spreadsheet with estimated cost, batch configs, and expected p50/p95 numbers based on your profile.
05:05 Ava Patel: any blockers for us to start?
05:07 Sophie Martin: just sign up, we'll provision credits and send the quickstart link. for VPC/dedicated we'll need a short checklist and the POC scope.
05:16 Jordan Kim: proposed POC success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms for typical queries, integration with our KMS for keys, and evidence of cost per 1k tokens below threshold we'll define.
05:28 Sophie Martin: perfect — can we say next steps are: send quickstart + creds, run initial bench, reconvene after bench with dedicated costing?
05:36 Ava Patel: yes, that works.
05:40 Sophie Martin: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the action items.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription some proper names mis-spelled in the text (e.g., kernel selection becomes colonel selection sometimes), occasional filler words removed for readability but many uh/um left to retain realism.
